message: Welcome everyone to today's session on Web Accessibility!
Excited to learn about this topic! I've been curious about how screen readers work.
Same here! I work with visually impaired students and want to make better learning materials.
Great to hear that motivation. Accessibility is one of the most impactful skills you can learn.
Is WCAG a legal requirement in Ethiopia?
Not yet a strict legal mandate, but it is increasingly adopted by government digital services and international organizations here.
What does the abbreviation a11y mean exactly?
a11y is a numeronym — 'a', then 11 letters, then 'y'. It stands for 'accessibility'.
That's clever! So i18n is internationalization?
Exactly right, Kidist!
How do screen readers handle Amharic text? Do they support Ethiopic script?
Great question. NVDA and VoiceOver have some Amharic support, though it's still improving. Proper lang attributes help a lot.
I never thought about alt text before. I always left the alt attribute empty.
Same! I used to put 'image' as the alt text for everything 😅
A common mistake! Alt text should describe what the image shows and why it matters in context.
What about decorative images? Do they need alt text too?
Decorative images should have an empty alt attribute — alt="" — so screen readers skip them.
I just tried navigating this page with keyboard only. It's harder than I expected!
Same experience here. Tab order really matters.
Can we use div and span for everything and just add ARIA roles?
That's an anti-pattern. The first rule of ARIA is: don't use ARIA if you can use a native HTML element instead. A <button> is always better than a <div role='button'>.
What contrast ratio tools do you recommend?
I recommend the WebAIM Contrast Checker, the axe browser extension, and Chrome DevTools' built-in contrast inspector.
Does anyone know if ALX courses themselves are accessible?
That's exactly what the Digital Bridge project is about — making ALX Savanna content accessible for all learners!
This is why captions matter so much. My cousin is deaf and struggles with most online courses.
Are auto-generated captions good enough?
Auto-captions are a starting point, but they need human review. They often miss technical terms and speaker identification.
What about audio descriptions for blind users? Most videos don't have them.
You're right, and that's a big gap. Our Digital Bridge player includes audio description support using the Web Speech API as a fallback.
